definitions.E16:
I’ll keep **Specialty Nursing (Emergency – Standard Option), Bachelor of Science in Nursing, Part-time** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor of Science in Nursing  
- **Study mode:** Part-time  
- **Delivery:** Fully online  
- **School:** School of Health Sciences  
- **Total credits:** 60.0  
- **Program focus:** Designed for registered nurses pursuing an emergency nursing specialty.

### Curriculum

**Required emergency nursing courses**
- **NSCC 7150 — Dysrhythmia Interpretation and Management** — 2 credits
- **NSER 7110 — Emergency Nursing Theory 1** — 4 credits
- **NSER 7210 — Emergency Nursing Theory 2** — 4 credits
- **NSER 7300 — Emergency Nursing Clinical 1** — 5 credits
- **NSER 7410 — Emergency Nursing Theory 3** — 4 credits
- **NSER 7500 — Emergency Nursing Clinical 2** — 5 credits

**Core and management component — 21 credits**
- **BUSA 7250 — Management Skills and Applications** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 7115 — Teaching and Learning in Specialty Nursing** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8000 — Systematic Inquiry** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8300 — Creative Leadership** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8500 — Professional Growth** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8600 — Community Nursing: Facilitating Health** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8800 — Community Nursing: Facilitating Health Action** — 3 credits

**Liberal Studies component — 12 credits**
- **COMM 7100 — Intercultural Communication Competency and Diversity Awareness for Professionals** — 3 credits
- **LIBS 7021 — Health Ethics** — 3 credits
- The remaining 6 credits are Liberal Studies electives from at least two academic disciplines, at the 100-level or higher.

**Elective pool**
You must complete **at least 3 credits from the approved pool**, rather than a fixed number of courses:
- **NSER 7250 — Advanced Cardiac Life Support** — 1 credit
- **NSER 7800 — Emergency Nursing and Mental Health** — 3 credits
- **NSSC 8130 — Independent Study in Specialty Nursing** — 3 credits

Other emergency-practice electives may be considered with Program Head approval.

### Entry requirements noted in the program record
The structured requirements include English Studies 12 at **73% or equivalent**, a post-secondary nursing diploma, current practicing RN registration, and at least **6 months of acute-care work experience**. Registration, resume documentation, clinical requirements, and some experience details require institutional confirmation.

For international applicants, the program record states that applicants must study from outside Canada or hold a valid Canadian work permit for the duration of clinical training. International applicants also require Program Head approval before applying. The program is not eligible for a study permit or PGWP under the stated restrictions.

definitions.E4:
Before applying to **Specialty Nursing (Emergency – Standard Option), Bachelor of Science in Nursing, Part-time**, know the following:

### Admission requirements
You should be prepared to provide:

- **English Studies 12 with at least 73%**, or an equivalent.
- A **post-secondary diploma in nursing**.
- Current practicing registration with the **BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM)**, a Canadian provincial equivalent, or an **RN licence number** if practicing outside Canada.
- At least **six months of acute-care work experience**.
- A **resume detailing your work experience**.

The program head may assess or waive some entry requirements. Experience outside acute care, or acute-care experience that is not recent, may require a refresher course. Contact the program head if you are unsure whether your qualifications or experience qualify.

### Clinical requirements
Before participating in clinical courses—**NSER 7300 — Emergency Nursing Clinical 1** and **NSER 7500 — Emergency Nursing Clinical 2**—you should expect to provide or complete:

- Current qualifying **CPR certification** from a Canadian provider, including a practical component.
- Proof of current professional registration.
- Respirator fit testing.
- Proof of influenza immunization or agreement to wear a mask during flu season.
- A completed clinical application.

Specific clinical-site requirements must be confirmed with the institution.

### If you are an international applicant
The program is available if you will complete it **outside Canada** or if you already have a Canadian work permit valid for the duration of clinical training. International applicants:

- Must receive **program head approval before applying**.
- Are **not eligible for a study permit** for this program.
- Should not assume the program qualifies for a **post-graduation work permit**; the stored program information says it is not PGWP-eligible.

### Timing and application notes
Applications are accepted throughout the year, with scheduled intakes in **January, April, and September**. Intakes may fill before the stated deadlines, so early application is recommended. After submitting a completed application, monitor your personal email and myBCIT account for application communications.

The program is **part-time and fully online**, but clinical components take place in clinical settings. Review the [program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-emergency-standard-option-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810bbsn/) and confirm any ambiguous requirements with BCIT or the program head.
definitions.E8:
For **international applicants**, the **Specialty Nursing (Emergency – Standard Option), Bachelor of Science in Nursing, Part-time** program is available only if you:

- Complete the program **from outside Canada**, or
- Hold a valid Canadian work permit that remains valid for the duration of your clinical training.

Important restrictions:

- You must receive **program head approval before applying**.
- This program does **not qualify for a study permit**.
- It is **not eligible for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP)**.
- The program is delivered fully online, but clinical training is required through **NSER 7300 — Emergency Nursing Clinical 1** and **NSER 7500 — Emergency Nursing Clinical 2**.

You must also provide evidence of the published entrance requirements, including:

- English Studies 12 at **73% or equivalent**
- A post-secondary nursing diploma
- Current RN registration or an RN licence number if practicing outside Canada
- At least **six months of acute-care experience**
- A resume

Clinical requirements include current qualifying CPR certification, professional registration, respirator fit testing, and compliance with the influenza immunization-or-masking policy. Some requirements require confirmation by BCIT or the program head.

[View the full program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-emergency-standard-option-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810bbsn/)

You must meet the English requirement:

- **English Studies 12 with at least 67%, or an equivalent qualification**

You must also meet **one** of these entry routes:

   - Minimum **2.8/4.0 GPA (70%)** across the final 30 undergraduate credits

2. **Alternate entry**
   - Bachelor’s degree in another discipline
   - Minimum **3.0/4.0 GPA (73%)** across the final 30 undergraduate credits
   - Significant computing knowledge gained through formal education and/or work experience
   - A completed **Pre-entry Assessment**
   - Program-area review; bridging courses may be required
   - A **Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire**

Applicants whose post-secondary studies were completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand require a comprehensive **ICES credential evaluation**; other Canadian evaluation services may be considered.

### Step 2: Department review

Complete applications are reviewed and ranked competitively by the Graduate Program Committee. Relevant industry experience is preferred but has no stated minimum threshold. Applicants may be asked for additional documents or an interview with the program area.

definitions.E26: The Master of Science Degree in Applied Computing gives you in-depth computing knowledge to solve complex real-world problems across industries and sectors. Through an interdisciplinary and rigorous full-time curriculum, you’ll be equipped to provide technical leadership in a professional setting or pursue further academic study. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing About the program Applied computing integrates information technology, computer science, and industry. You’ll take courses in core computing, and you will have the opportunity to work in an application area in another discipline. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how advanced computing, tools, and computational methods can be applied in practice to overcome challenges and create efficiencies. The program employs a cohort model, with the same group in all courses. This allows you to work through the program together, sharing your experience and expertise and building industry connections that will last long after you graduate 1 intake: September 4 15-week terms, normally completed over two academic years full time First year with two terms , delivered in-person, including: Algorithm analysis Human-centered Computing Machine Learning (ML) & Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Science Cybersecurity Research methods Second year on thesis path or internship & project path Based on BCIT Burnaby Campus, and possibly the Downtown Campus or field locations where appropriate. You’ll be uniquely qualified to apply your knowledge and skills in various areas, such as: computational science rehabilitation engineering building science biotechnology autonomous vehicles sustainability smart micro-grids social impacts of technology network security an approved project area of your choosing based on your professional background See the Program Details to learn more. Who it’s for This degree might be for you if you: Are inspired to maximize the societal benefit of computing by solving real-world issues Would like to apply your skills in industry after graduation, but might also consider applying for a PhD Are looking for a cohort-based program where you’ll work with other students to share problem-solving skills and approaches, as you would in a work setting Have an applied problem you believe could be improved through computing Would like to study with computing faculty, application experts outside of computing, and industry partners Students will also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to gain additional knowledge in a specific application area. Please review the Entrance Requirements to learn more. What grads can do Provide technical leadership for software/system development teams Demonstrate deep, critical knowledge and understanding of advanced topics in computing science Analyze how computing systems and software can be used in practical applications and interdisciplinary fields Design, develop, and implement innovative solutions to industry problems with consideration to relevant ethical, social and environmental issues Explain and advocate for applied computing solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences in both business and academic settings See the Graduating & Jobs page to learn more. definitions.E28: This degree focuses on Applied Computing, which is fundamentally related to applying computing technology and computational methods to derive solutions to complex practical problems. Course work will emphasize current issues in industry, case studies, and applied research projects. This program offers you a chance to work with an interdisciplinary and diverse team of academic supervisors that may include faculty from Computing, faculty from an application domain, as well as industry practitioners. You’ll also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to explore a specific application area. For more information about faculty, visit the Faculty, Advisors & Staff page. Applied research is fundamental to the program. Two paths are offered, diverging in second year: Thesis Path – Path 1: complete a thesis project and defend it in your second year. You’ll need to demonstrate originality in the application of your knowledge, either through new publishable research, or a novel solution to an existing practical problem. This is the best path if you’re interested in possibly pursuing a future Ph.D. Project & Internship Path – Path 2: a one-semester research project with a one-semester internship, which may be paid or unpaid. The internship will involve an external company or a BCIT lab where you can learn how advanced computing techniques are applied to solve interdisciplinary problems. The research project may be done in collaboration with the sponsor from the internship, providing added value in terms of practical utility. Students will also complete a 3-credit special topics course, covering emerging areas in Applied Computing, such as Quantum Computing, Generative AI, or Deep Learning. Both paths will require students to: examine literature in a related discipline, recognize gaps and limitations in existing technologies and processes, organize and plan their approach, and demonstrate competence in applying advanced techniques to solve problems. In both paths, students will present a written argument that addresses a complex problem in applied computing. Did you miss our Info Session? Please see the recording from October 2024: BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing | Info Session Program length Two years, full-time. The maximum time to complete this program is five years.
